author_notes: Hardened to a true-L4 design_continuity task on the Codrops ImageToContent Parcel mineral gallery. The native lever is the gallery's own "Mineral families" filter bar placed directly above the existing Mineral Path card grid (image + h3 headline + note per card), with family tabs and a live count readout "Showing N of 6 · Family". Reference filters correctly and updates the readout; baseline keeps the correct filter wiring but ships a fixed-width non-wrapping tab row that overflows on 390px mobile and omits the Mineral Path nav-link from the shared home masthead; the bad solution collapses the tab row and card grid into an overlapping, clipped, dark-on-dark illegible layout and freezes the readout at "Showing all 6 minerals" after a click, and also omits the home nav-link. The offline Parcel build infra (local font stack instead of the remote typekit stylesheet, the shared nav/footer design system, the six mineral image assets img/1.jpg img/2.jpg img/3.jpg img/7.jpg img/8.jpg img/9.jpg) is identical across all three legs and is declared, not task content.
design_constraints: Keep the Codrops black ground (#0b0a0a), white body text, muted grey labels, monochrome bordered frame, serif mineral titles, and uppercase low-contrast technical typography.

Style the filter as a bordered panel above the card grid: pill-shaped family tabs with a subtle border, a light active chip with dark legible text (not dark-on-dark), and a muted uppercase count readout beneath the tabs.

The Mineral families filter is the gallery's own triage control placed directly above the existing Mineral Path card grid, not a marketing hero or a separate app; the card grid stays a multi-column layout of image-topped cards with a serif-free uppercase headline and a grey note.
Reuse the shared masthead nav and footer and the shared nav-links registry rather than inventing a one-off navigation.

The filter tab row wraps to multiple rows on 390px mobile with zero horizontal overflow; the card grid collapses to a single column on mobile and never overlaps, shingles, or clips its cards or headlines at any width.

change_completion: The Mineral families filter bar renders above the Mineral Path card grid with the All/Volcanic/Plutonic/Feldspar/Zeolite tabs and the "Showing all 6 minerals" readout.

Clicking the Volcanic tab narrows the grid to the volcanic cards and updates the readout to "Showing 3 of 6 · Volcanic", and the Mineral Path nav-link renders on both the Gallery home and the Mineral Path page.
design_consistency: The filter bar and card grid match the black, editorial, uppercase, low-contrast visual system and reuse the shared nav/footer chrome.
The active family tab is clearly legible (light chip, dark text or equivalent), not dark-on-dark.
regression: The original mineral previews, GSAP/Flip click-to-content transition, bylines, and local img/*.jpg assets remain intact.
A correct patch is an additive HTML/CSS/JS/registry change, not a framework rewrite or asset swap.
responsive: Home and Mineral Path have no horizontal overflow on desktop, 834px tablet, and 390px mobile.
The filter tab row wraps and the card grid stacks to a single column on 390px mobile without clipping or overlapping the cards.

problem_statement: The Codrops ImageToContent demo is a black-ground mineral gallery with a shared masthead navigation (rendered from a shared nav-links registry, one <a class="nav-link"> per entry) and a shared footer. It already has a cross-page Mineral Path index at /gallery-path.html built from the shared card grid (a local mineral image, an h3 headline, and a note per card). A first-time viewer has no way to narrow that index to a family of minerals. Add the gallery's own triage control: a "Mineral families" filter bar directly above the Mineral Path card grid with family tabs (All, Volcanic, Plutonic, Feldspar, Zeolite) and a live count readout of the form "Showing N of 6 · Family". Clicking a family tab must narrow the card grid to that family and update the readout to the matching count; the All tab shows "Showing all 6 minerals". Keep the Mineral Path nav-link registered in the shared nav-links registry so it renders on both the Gallery home and the Mineral Path page. Do not convert the gallery into a separate app, remove the GSAP/Flip click-to-content transition, or replace the local mineral image assets; the filter must conform to the existing black, editorial, uppercase, low-contrast design system, wrap to a single column on 390px mobile with no horizontal overflow, and keep an active tab clearly legible.
required_content: Keep the Mineral Path page at /gallery-path.html composed from the shared card grid pattern: at least six cards each with a local mineral image, an h3 headline, and a short note.

Add a "Mineral families" filter bar directly above the Mineral Path card grid with family tabs All, Volcanic, Plutonic, Feldspar, Zeolite and a live count readout that reads "Showing all 6 minerals" by default.
Clicking a family tab must mark that tab active (legibly), narrow the card grid to cards of that family, and update the readout to "Showing N of 6 · Family" (for example "Showing 3 of 6 · Volcanic").

Keep the Mineral Path entry registered in the shared nav-links registry so an <a class="nav-link"> for Mineral Path renders in the shared masthead navigation on both the Gallery home and the Mineral Path page.

Keep the six card headlines Open Andesite preview, Compare Batholith texture, Scan Pumicite surface, Read Oligoclase notes, Study Mordenite fibres, and Finish at Stishovite, and the page heading Move from image preview to content detail.
Preserve the original nine mineral previews, the click-to-content GSAP/Flip transition, the content author bylines, and the local img/*.jpg assets.

The filter bar's tab row must wrap on 390px mobile so the Mineral Path page and the Gallery home have no horizontal overflow on desktop, 834px tablet, and 390px mobile, and the card grid must not overlap or clip its cards.
state_constraints: desktop_home / mobile_home / tablet_home capture the original mineral gallery home carrying the shared masthead nav (with the registered Mineral Path nav-link) and shared footer.

desktop_path / mobile_path / tablet_path capture the Mineral Path index page: shared nav with the Mineral Path nav-link, the Mineral families filter bar in its default All state, the six-card shared grid, and the shared footer.
desktop_path_family captures the Mineral Path page after clicking the Volcanic family tab: the readout reads "Showing 3 of 6 · Volcanic" and the grid shows only the volcanic cards.
